Undo the existing system-wide install (on each host)\n\nThe official install script put things in `/usr/local`. Remove those first:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop ollama 2>/dev/null\nsudo systemctl disable ollama 2>/dev/null\nsudo rm -f /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service\nsudo rm -f /usr/local/bin/ollama\nsudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/ollama\n```\n\nIf the script created an `ollama` user/group, you can leave them or `sudo userdel ollama && sudo groupdel ollama`.\n\n## 2. Install manually to `/home/sora/programs/ollama/`\n\nDon't re-run `install.sh` — it's hard-wired for `/usr/local`. Extract the tarball yourself:\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p /home/sora/programs/ollama\ncd /home/sora/programs/ollama\ncurl -L https://ollama.com/download/ollama-linux-amd64.tgz -o ollama.tgz\ntar -xzf ollama.tgz\nrm ollama.tgz\n```\n\nYou'll end up with `/home/sora/programs/ollama/bin/ollama` and `/home/sora/programs/ollama/lib/ollama/`.\n\nQuick sanity check:\n\n```bash\n/home/sora/programs/ollama/bin/ollama --version\n```\n\n## 3. Write a launcher script (per host, with the right IP)\n\nSave this as `/home/sora/programs/ollama/serve.sh`. **Set `BIND_IP` to `192.168.1.11`, `.12`, or `.13` depending on the host:**\n\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\nDIR=\"/home/sora/programs/ollama\"\nBIND_IP=\"192.168.1.11\"   # change to .12 on host 2, .13 on host 3\nPORT=\"10000\"\n\nexport OLLAMA_HOST=\"${BIND_IP}:${PORT}\"\nexport OLLAMA_MODELS=\"${DIR}/models\"\nexport PATH=\"${DIR}/bin:${PATH}\"\n\nmkdir -p \"${OLLAMA_MODELS}\"\nexec \"${DIR}/bin/ollama\" serve\n```\n\nMake it executable: `chmod +x /home/sora/programs/ollama/serve.sh`\n\n## 4. Run it as a systemd service (recommended)\n\nCreate `/etc/systemd/system/ollama.service`:\n\n```ini\n[Unit]\nDescription=Ollama (sora)\nAfter=network-online.target\nWants=network-online.target\n\n[Service]\nType=simple\nUser=sora\nGroup=sora\nExecStart=/home/sora/programs/ollama/serve.sh\nRestart=on-failure\nRestartSec=3\n\n[Install]\nWantedBy=multi-user.target\n```\n\nThen:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl daemon-reload\nsudo systemctl enable --now ollama\nsudo systemctl status ollama\n```\n\nIf you don't want systemd, just run `nohup /home/sora/programs/ollama/serve.sh > /tmp/ollama.log 2>&1 &`.\n\n## 5. Verify from another machine\n\nFrom any of the three hosts (or your dev box):\n\n```bash\ncurl http://192.168.1.11:10000/api/tags\ncurl http://192.168.1.12:10000/api/tags\ncurl http://192.168.1.13:10000/api/tags\n```\n\nEach should return JSON (likely `{\"models\":[]}` until you pull one).\n\n## 6. Pull a model on each host\n\nThe CLI also needs `OLLAMA_HOST` so it talks to the right server:\n\n```bash\nOLLAMA_HOST=192.168.1.11:10000 /home/sora/programs/ollama/bin/ollama pull llama3.2\n```\n\n## Per-host summary\n\n| Host | BIND_IP in serve.sh |\n|---|---|\n| sora-1 | `192.168.1.11` |\n| sora-2 | `192.168.1.12` |\n| sora-3 | `192.168.1.13` |\n\nEverything else is identical across the three.\n\n## Things to watch for\n\n- **Firewall**: if these hosts have one, open TCP 10000 (e.g. `sudo ufw allow 10000/tcp` or the nftables equivalent).\n- **The IP must already be bound to an interface on the host.** Check with `ip addr` — `OLLAMA_HOST=192.168.1.11:10000` only works on the host that actually owns `192.168.1.11`. If you want one config for all three hosts, you can use `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:10000` instead and let each host bind to all its interfaces.\n- **CPU-only mode**: the warning is fine — Ollama will work, just slowly. If these are eventually getting GPUs, you'll want to reinstall the matching CUDA/ROCm libs.\n\nWant me to write a single setup script you can scp+run on each host, parameterized by `BIND_IP`?"

        "type":"text",
        "text":"Yes — Alpine has three differences that bite here:\n\n## 1. Ollama is built against glibc; Alpine uses musl\n\nThe `ollama-linux-amd64.tgz` you downloaded is a glibc binary. It will fail to start on Alpine with something like `not found` (which is actually the dynamic linker complaining, not the file missing). Install the glibc shim:\n\n```bash\napk add gcompat libstdc++ libgcc curl\n```\n\n`gcompat` provides a glibc-compatible loader; the other two cover the C++ runtime Ollama links against. Test after installing:\n\n```bash\n/home/sora/programs/ollama/bin/ollama --version\n```\n\nIf it prints a version, you're good. If you still get loader errors, the heavier alternative is `apk add --no-cache build-base go cmake git` and build Ollama from source — but try `gcompat` first, it usually just works.\n\n> Aside: that \"API is now available at 127.0.0.1:11434\" message from the official `install.sh` is printed unconditionally — it doesn't mean the daemon actually started under Alpine. Don't trust it.\n\n## 2. Alpine uses OpenRC, not systemd\n\nReplace my systemd unit with an OpenRC init script. Save as `/etc/init.d/ollama`:\n\n```sh\n#!/sbin/openrc-run\n\nname=\"ollama\"\ndescription=\"Ollama LLM server\"\n\ncommand=\"/home/sora/programs/ollama/serve.sh\"\ncommand_user=\"sora:sora\"\ncommand_background=true\npidfile=\"/run/ollama.pid\"\noutput_log=\"/var/log/ollama.log\"\nerror_log=\"/var/log/ollama.log\"\n\ndepend() {\n    need net\n    after firewall\n}\n```\n\nThen:\n\n```bash\nchmod +x /etc/init.d/ollama\nrc-update add ollama default\nrc-service ollama start\nrc-service ollama status\n```\n\nLogs land in `/var/log/ollama.log` instead of `journalctl`.\n\n## 3. Firewall — no `ufw` on Alpine\n\nAlpine ships with no firewall enabled by default. If you've set one up, it's most likely `awall` over nftables. Two cases:\n\n**No firewall configured:** nothing to do, port 10000 is already open.\n\n**awall in use:** add a policy in `/etc/awall/optional/ollama.json`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"filter\": [\n    { \"in\": \"internet\", \"out\": \"_fw\", \"service\": \"ollama\", \"action\": \"accept\" }\n  ],\n  \"service\": {\n    \"ollama\": [ { \"proto\": \"tcp\", \"port\": 10000 } ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThen `awall enable ollama && awall activate`.\n\n**Raw nftables:** `nft add rule inet filter input tcp dport 10000 accept` and persist via `/etc/nftables.nft`.\n\n## 4. Minor: user creation if `sora` doesn't exist yet\n\nAlpine's `adduser` is the busybox variant:\n\n```bash\nadduser -D -h /home/sora -s /bin/sh sora\n```\n\n`-D` skips password prompt. Add to a group with `addgroup sora <group>`.\n\n## 5. Everything else stays the same\n\nThe tarball extraction, the `serve.sh` launcher, the `OLLAMA_HOST` / `OLLAMA_MODELS` env vars, the per-host IP table, the `curl /api/tags` verification — all unchanged.\n\n---\n\n**Alternative if `gcompat` gives you trouble:** run Ollama in Docker instead of bare-metal. `apk add docker docker-cli && rc-update add docker default && rc-service docker start`, then:\n\n```bash\ndocker run -d --restart=always \\\n  -v /home/sora/programs/ollama/models:/root/.ollama \\\n  -p 192.168.1.11:10000:11434 \\\n  --name ollama \\\n  ollama/ollama\n```\n\nThe container is glibc-based internally, so musl is no longer your problem. From the host you built on:\n\n```bash\nscp /home/sora/programs/ollama/bin/ollama sora@192.168.1.12:/home/sora/programs/ollama/bin/\nscp /home/sora/programs/ollama/bin/ollama sora@192.168.1.13:/home/sora/programs/ollama/bin/\n```\n\nDon't forget `apk add libstdc++ libgcc` on hosts 2 and 3 before running.\n\n## Everything from the earlier setup still applies\n\n`serve.sh`, the OpenRC init script, the per-host `BIND_IP` table, the `curl /api/tags` check — all unchanged.         "text":"Three things to unpack:\n\n## 1. The missing `go` package\n\nAlpine's `apk search` only matches the start of the name by default, and only against your enabled+updated index. What I'd check first:\n\n```bash\napk update\napk search '^go$'\n```\n\nIf `go` still doesn't show up, your `community` repo line probably points at an Alpine version that doesn't carry it (older or `edge`-only). Check `/etc/apk/repositories`:\n\n```bash\ncat /etc/apk/repositories\n```\n\nYou want a line like `https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.21/community` (or whatever Alpine version matches `/etc/alpine-release`). If only `main` is enabled, add the matching `community` line, then `apk update` again.\n\n`gcc-go` (which you found) is GCC's gccgo frontend — it usually lags upstream Go by a major version and has known issues with newer Go features Ollama uses. Don't substitute it.\n\nIf community is enabled, indexed, and `go` is genuinely absent in your Alpine version, the only musl-pure fallback is bootstrapping Go from source (slow, ~30 min). I won't bake that into the script — fix the package availability first.\n\n## 2. Always-static build\n\nTwo flag groups matter:\n\n- **C++ runtime static**: `-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc` via `CGO_LDFLAGS`. The C++ pulled in by llama.cpp's cgo bindings is the part that defaults to dynamic.\n- **Final link static**: `-linkmode external -extldflags '-static'` in Go ldflags. This forces musl itself to be statically linked too.\n\nThe result should pass `ldd ./ollama` with `not a dynamic executable`. If it doesn't, that's a real build problem, not a cosmetic one — and the script bails out.\n\n## 3. The script\n\nSave as `/home/sora/programs/ollama/build-and-deploy.sh` on the build host. Config at the top, peer IPs configurable. Skips the rebuild if the version on disk already matches GitHub's latest release.\n\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\n# ollama-build-and-deploy.sh\n#\n# Build a fully static, musl-linked ollama binary on Alpine, then ship the\n# source tree and the compiled binary to two peer hosts. If the most recent\n# upstream release tag already matches the version we have on disk, the build\n# step is skipped — but the deploy step still runs (idempotent at the peer).\n#\n# Why this shape: we want one build host doing the heavy lifting, and the\n# peers receiving both the binary AND the source so any of them can rebuild\n# without depending on this script being re-run. Hardware is identical across\n# the three hosts, so the binary is portable.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\n# {{{ config — override DIR via $1 if you want a different install root\nDIR=\"${1:-/home/sora/programs/ollama}\"\n\nPEER_1=\"192.168.1.12\"\nPEER_2=\"192.168.1.13\"\nPEER_USER=\"sora\"\n\nSRC_DIR=\"${DIR}/src\"\nBIN_DIR=\"${DIR}/bin\"\nDIST_DIR=\"${DIR}/dist\"\nLOG_DIR=\"${DIR}/tmp\"\n\nVERSION_FILE=\"${DIR}/.built-version\"\nOLLAMA_REPO=\"https://github.com/ollama/ollama.git\"\nGITHUB_API=\"https://api.github.com/repos/ollama/ollama/releases/latest\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ setup_dirs()\n# Create the on-disk layout. The log directory is symlinked into /tmp so build\n# noise stays in RAM rather than wearing the disk.\nsetup_dirs() {\n    mkdir -p \"${DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${BIN_DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${DIST_DIR}\"\n    if [ ! -L \"${LOG_DIR}\" ]; then\n        local ram_log=\"/tmp/ollama-build-$(id -u)\"\n        mkdir -p \"${ram_log}\"\n        ln -snf \"${ram_log}\" \"${LOG_DIR}\"\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ ensure_build_deps()\n# build-base = gcc+g+++make; cmake for llama.cpp; git+bash+curl for plumbing.\n# go must already be installed via apk — if it isn't, we stop here so the user\n# can fix the community-repo situation rather than have the script silently\n# fall back to a glibc Go shim.\nensure_build_deps() {\n    apk add --no-cache build-base cmake git bash curl\n    if ! command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        echo \"ERROR: 'go' is not installed.\" >&2\n        echo \"Try: apk update && apk add go\" >&2\n        echo \"If apk doesn't find it, enable the community repo for your\" >&2\n        echo \"Alpine version in /etc/apk/repositories and apk update.\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ get_latest_tag()\n# Ask GitHub for the most recent published release tag. We don't trust git\n# ls-remote here because it would include pre-release and draft tags.\nget_latest_tag() {\n    local response\n    response=\"$(curl -fsSL \"${GITHUB_API}\")\"\n    local tag\n    tag=\"$(echo \"${response}\" | sed -n 's/.*\"tag_name\": *\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n    if [ -z \"${tag}\" ]; then\n        echo \"ERROR: could not parse latest tag from GitHub API\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    echo \"${tag}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ already_built()\n# True if .built-version matches the desired tag AND the binary still exists.\n# Either condition failing forces a rebuild — we don't want a stale tag file\n# to mask a missing binary.\nalready_built() {\n    local target_tag=\"$1\"\n    if [ ! -f \"${VERSION_FILE}\" ]; then\n        return 1\n    fi\n    if [ ! -x \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" ]; then\n        return 1\n    fi\n    local built_tag\n    built_tag=\"$(cat \"${VERSION_FILE}\")\"\n    [ \"${built_tag}\" = \"${target_tag}\" ]\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ fetch_source()\n# Shallow clone at the exact tag. Previous checkout is wiped so we never carry\n# half-built artifacts from a prior failed run into a new attempt.\nfetch_source() {\n    local tag=\"$1\"\n    rm -rf \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n    git clone --depth=1 --branch \"${tag}\" \"${OLLAMA_REPO}\" \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ build_static()\n# Two-step build:\n#   1. `make` invokes CMake for llama.cpp (produces static .a archives) and\n#      then go build for the ollama binary. We pre-set CGO_LDFLAGS so the C++\n#      runtime gets pulled in statically.\n#   2. We rebuild the Go binary explicitly with -linkmode external and\n#      -extldflags '-static', because the upstream Makefile's go invocation\n#      doesn't pass those through.\n# Final `ldd` check is non-negotiable: if it isn't fully static, we bail loudly\n# rather than ship a binary that needs runtime libs the peers might lack.\nbuild_static() {\n    cd \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n\n    export CGO_ENABLED=1\n    export CC=gcc\n    export CXX=g++\n    export CGO_CFLAGS=\"-O2\"\n    export CGO_CXXFLAGS=\"-O2\"\n    export CGO_LDFLAGS=\"-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc\"\n\n    local build_log=\"${LOG_DIR}/build.log\"\n    make -j\"$(nproc)\" >\"${build_log}\" 2>&1\n\n    go build \\\n        -tags 'netgo osusergo' \\\n        -ldflags '-linkmode external -extldflags \"-static\"' \\\n        -o \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" \\\n        .\n\n    local ldd_out\n    ldd_out=\"$(ldd \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" 2>&1 || true)\"\n    if echo \"${ldd_out}\" | grep -q 'not a dynamic'; then\n        echo \"OK: binary is fully static.\"\n    else\n        echo \"ERROR: binary still has dynamic dependencies:\" >&2\n        echo \"${ldd_out}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ package_dist()\n# Bundle the source tree AND the compiled binary into one tarball, so peers\n# receive everything needed to either run as-is or rebuild from source.\npackage_dist() {\n    local tag=\"$1\"\n    local archive_name=\"ollama-${tag}.tar.gz\"\n    local archive_path=\"${DIST_DIR}/${archive_name}\"\n    rm -f \"${archive_path}\"\n    tar -czf \"${archive_path}\" \\\n        -C \"${DIR}\" \\\n        --transform \"s,^src,ollama-${tag}/src,\" \\\n        --transform \"s,^bin,ollama-${tag}/bin,\" \\\n        src bin\n    echo \"Packaged: ${archive_path}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ peer_already_has_version()\n# Cheap remote check so we don't re-scp a multi-hundred-MB tarball when the\n# peer is already current. If ssh fails, the peer is treated as out-of-date.\npeer_already_has_version() {\n    local peer=\"$1\"\n    local target_tag=\"$2\"\n    local peer_version\n    peer_version=\"$(ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \\\n        \"cat ${DIR}/.built-version 2>/dev/null || echo none\" 2>/dev/null || echo none)\"\n    [ \"${peer_version}\" = \"${target_tag}\" ]\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ deploy_to_peer()\n# Copies tarball to the peer, extracts in place, replaces src/ and bin/,\n# records the version. Peer runtime config (serve.sh, openrc unit) is NOT\n# touched here — that's a separate one-time provisioning concern.\ndeploy_to_peer() {\n    local peer=\"$1\"\n    local tag=\"$2\"\n    local archive_name=\"ollama-${tag}.tar.gz\"\n    local archive_path=\"${DIST_DIR}/${archive_name}\"\n\n    if peer_already_has_version \"${peer}\" \"${tag}\"; then\n        echo \"Peer ${peer} already at ${tag}, skipping.\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n\n    echo \"Deploying ${tag} to ${peer}...\"\n    ssh \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \"mkdir -p ${DIR}\"\n    scp \"${archive_path}\" \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}:${DIR}/\"\n    ssh \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \"\n        set -e\n        cd ${DIR}\n        tar -xzf ${archive_name}\n        rm -rf src bin\n        mv ollama-${tag}/src .\n        mv ollama-${tag}/bin .\n        rmdir ollama-${tag}\n        echo ${tag} > .built-version\n        rm -f ${archive_name}\n    \"\n    echo \"Peer ${peer} updated to ${tag}.\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ main\nmain() {\n    setup_dirs\n    ensure_build_deps\n\n    local tag\n    tag=\"$(get_latest_tag)\"\n    echo \"Latest upstream release: ${tag}\"\n\n    if already_built \"${tag}\"; then\n        echo \"Local build already at ${tag}, skipping rebuild.\"\n    else\n        fetch_source \"${tag}\"\n        build_static\n        echo \"${tag}\" > \"${VERSION_FILE}\"\n        echo \"Local build complete: ${tag}\"\n    fi\n\n    package_dist \"${tag}\"\n    deploy_to_peer \"${PEER_1}\" \"${tag}\"\n    deploy_to_peer \"${PEER_2}\" \"${tag}\"\n\n    echo \"All hosts at ${tag}.\"\n}\n# }}}\n\nmain \"$@\"\n```\n\n## Caveats worth flagging up front\n\n- **Static link verification is the canary.** If the `ldd` check fails after the first run, that's the signal that something in llama.cpp's link line refuses to honor `-static`. Most likely culprit is a CMake-generated link command that hard-codes a shared lib. The build log at `/home/sora/programs/ollama/tmp/build.log` will show which library complained.\n- **The second `go build` pass duplicates work.** I'd rather pay that cost than try to thread static-link flags into Ollama's Makefile, which the upstream project rewrites often.\n- **SSH key auth assumed.** The deploy step won't survive a password prompt — set up `ssh-copy-id sora@192.168.1.12` and `.13` from the build host first.\n- **The `gcc-static` / `libstdc++-static` situation on Alpine is fuzzy.** On most Alpine versions, `build-base` already includes the static archives. If the link complains about missing `libstdc++.a`, try `apk add g++ --no-cache` explicitly, or check `find / -name 'libstdc++.a' 2>/dev/null` to see where the static lib is.\n\nWant me to add a separate one-time provisioning script that lays down `serve.sh` + the OpenRC unit + the per-host `BIND_IP` on each peer, so the build/deploy script can stay focused on just the binary?"
      }]

          "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# ollama-build-and-deploy.sh\n#\n# Bootstrap a fully musl-native toolchain on Alpine, then build a fully-static\n# Ollama binary, then ship the source tree and the compiled binary to two\n# peer hosts.\n#\n# Strategy:\n#   stage 0 : install build deps (gcc, g++, cmake, git, curl, ...)\n#   stage 1 : bootstrap Go from nothing on musl\n#               Go 1.4 (C source) -> Go 1.17.13 -> Go 1.20.14 -> Go 1.22.x\n#             Each stage produces the bootstrap input for the next. All\n#             stages are cached on disk so reruns only redo what's missing.\n#   stage 2 : ask GitHub for the latest stable Ollama tag.\n#             Bail out of the rebuild if .built-version already matches and\n#             a binary exists.\n#   stage 3 : clone Ollama at that tag. Ollama vendors llama.cpp, so this\n#             one clone covers both.\n#   stage 4 : build with full static link flags. Verify with ldd. Bail\n#             loudly if the binary still has dynamic dependencies — we'd\n#             rather notice now than discover it when a peer can't run it.\n#   stage 5 : tar (source tree + binary) into one archive.\n#   stage 6 : scp + extract on two peer hosts. Skip per-peer if that peer\n#             already has the same tag recorded.\n#\n# Run from any directory. First positional arg overrides the install root.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\n# {{{ config\nDIR=\"${1:-/home/sora/programs/ollama}\"\n\nPEER_1=\"192.168.1.12\"\nPEER_2=\"192.168.1.13\"\nPEER_USER=\"sora\"\n\n# subdirectory layout\nBOOTSTRAP_DIR=\"${DIR}/go-bootstrap\"\nGO14_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go1.4\"\nGO17_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go1.17.13\"\nGO20_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go1.20.14\"\nGO_FINAL_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go-final\"\n\nSRC_DIR=\"${DIR}/src\"\nBIN_DIR=\"${DIR}/bin\"\nDIST_DIR=\"${DIR}/dist\"\nLOG_DIR=\"${DIR}/tmp\"\nDOWNLOAD_DIR=\"${DIR}/downloads\"\n\nVERSION_FILE=\"${DIR}/.built-version\"\nOLLAMA_REPO=\"https://github.com/ollama/ollama.git\"\nGITHUB_API=\"https://api.github.com/repos/ollama/ollama/releases/latest\"\n\n# Go versions for the bootstrap chain. The pinned final version is what we\n# actually use to compile Ollama; bump it when Ollama requires newer Go.\nGO14_TARBALL=\"go1.4-bootstrap-20171003.tar.gz\"\nGO17_TARBALL=\"go1.17.13.src.tar.gz\"\nGO20_TARBALL=\"go1.20.14.src.tar.gz\"\nGO_FINAL_VERSION=\"1.22.10\"\nGO_FINAL_TARBALL=\"go${GO_FINAL_VERSION}.src.tar.gz\"\n\nGO_DL_BASE=\"https://go.dev/dl\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ setup_dirs()\n# Create the on-disk layout. The log directory is a symlink into /tmp so\n# build noise stays in RAM rather than chewing disk.\nsetup_dirs() {\n    mkdir -p \"${DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${BIN_DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${DIST_DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${DOWNLOAD_DIR}\"\n    if [ ! -L \"${LOG_DIR}\" ]; then\n        local ram_log=\"/tmp/ollama-build-$(id -u)\"\n        mkdir -p \"${ram_log}\"\n        ln -snf \"${ram_log}\" \"${LOG_DIR}\"\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ ensure_build_deps()\n# Native build tools only — we are deliberately NOT installing go from apk,\n# because the whole point of this script is to bootstrap Go from source.\n# linux-headers is needed by some of llama.cpp's C bits.\nensure_build_deps() {\n    apk add --no-cache \\\n        build-base \\\n        cmake \\\n        git \\\n        bash \\\n        curl \\\n        linux-headers \\\n        ca-certificates\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ download_if_missing()\n# Idempotent download into ${DOWNLOAD_DIR}. We keep the tarballs around so\n# repeated runs don't refetch — also useful if a later bootstrap stage fails\n# and you want to retry without redownloading.\ndownload_if_missing() {\n    local filename=\"$1\"\n    local dest=\"${DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${filename}\"\n    if [ -f \"${dest}\" ]; then\n        return 0\n    fi\n    local url=\"${GO_DL_BASE}/${filename}\"\n    echo \"Fetching ${url}\"\n    curl -fsSL \"${url}\" -o \"${dest}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ extract_to()\n# Untar a Go source tarball into a target directory. Go's tarballs always\n# extract a top-level \"go/\" folder; we rename it to the version-specific\n# install root so we can keep all stages side-by-side.\nextract_to() {\n    local tarball_name=\"$1\"\n    local target_root=\"$2\"\n    local tarball=\"${DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${tarball_name}\"\n    rm -rf \"${target_root}\"\n    local staging\n    staging=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\n    tar -xzf \"${tarball}\" -C \"${staging}\"\n    mv \"${staging}/go\" \"${target_root}\"\n    rmdir \"${staging}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ build_go14()\n# Go 1.4 is the last C-based Go. See ${gobuildlog}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    }\n\n    local ldd_out\n    ldd_out=\"$(ldd \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" 2>&1 || true)\"\n    if echo \"${ldd_out}\" | grep -q 'not a dynamic'; then\n        echo \"OK: binary is fully static.\"\n    else\n        echo \"ERROR: binary still has dynamic dependencies:\" >&2\n        echo \"${ldd_out}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ package_dist()\n# Bundle the source tree AND the compiled binary together. Wipes any previous checkout first so\n# stale artifacts from a failed earlier run can't poison the build.\nfetch_ollama_source() {\n    local tag=\"$1\"\n    rm -rf \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n    git clone --depth=1 --branch \"${tag}\" \"${OLLAMA_REPO}\" \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ build_static()\n# Two-phase build:\n#   phase A: `make` lets Ollama's upstream Makefile drive CMake for llama.cpp\n#            and produces the .a archives. CGO_LDFLAGS pre-sets the static\n#            C++ runtime flags so the cgo compile picks them up.\n#   phase B: rebuild the Go binary explicitly with -linkmode external and\n#            -extldflags '-static'. Ollama's Makefile invokes go build without\n#            these flags, so we re-do that step ourselves.\n#\n# Verification is non-negotiable: ldd must report \"not a dynamic executable\".\n# If it doesn't, we bail out — better to fail here than ship a binary that\n# silently depends on libs the peers might not have.\nbuild_static() {\n    cd \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n\n    export CGO_ENABLED=1\n    export CC=gcc\n    export CXX=g++\n    export CGO_CFLAGS=\"-O2\"\n    export CGO_CXXFLAGS=\"-O2\"\n    export CGO_LDFLAGS=\"-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc\"\n\n    local makelog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-make.log\"\n    make -j\"$(nproc)\" >\"${makelog}\" 2>&1 || {\n        echo \"ERROR: make failed. See ${makelog}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    }\n\n    local gobuildlog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-go-build.log\"\n    go build \\\n        -tags 'netgo osusergo' \\\n        -ldflags '-linkmode external -extldflags \"-static\"' \\\n        -o \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" \\\n        . >\"${gobuildlog}\" 2>&1 || {\n        echo \"ERROR: go build failed. See ${gobuildlog}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    }\n\n    local ldd_out\n    ldd_out=\"$(ldd \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" 2>&1 || true)\"\n    if echo \"${ldd_out}\" | grep -q 'not a dynamic'; then\n        echo \"OK: binary is fully static.\"\n    else\n        echo \"ERROR: binary still has dynamic dependencies:\" >&2\n        echo \"${ldd_out}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ package_dist()\n# Bundle the source tree AND the compiled binary together. Peers get both\n# so they can either run as-is or rebuild from source themselves.\npackage_dist() {\n    local tag=\"$1\"\n    local archive_name=\"ollama-${tag}.tar.gz\"\n    local archive_path=\"${DIST_DIR}/${archive_name}\"\n    rm -f \"${archive_path}\"\n    tar -czf \"${archive_path}\" \\\n        -C \"${DIR}\" \\\n        --transform \"s,^src,ollama-${tag}/src,\" \\\n        --transform \"s,^bin,ollama-${tag}/bin,\" \\\n        src bin\n    echo \"Packaged: ${archive_path}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ peer_already_has_version()\n# Cheap remote check so we don't re-scp when the peer is already current.\n# Network or ssh failure is treated as \"not current\" — better to over-deploy\n# than to skip a peer that's actually out of date.\npeer_already_has_version() {\n    local peer=\"$1\"\n    local target_tag=\"$2\"\n    local peer_version\n    peer_version=\"$(ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \\\n        \"cat ${DIR}/.built-version 2>/dev/null || echo none\" 2>/dev/null || echo none)\"\n    [ \"${peer_version}\" = \"${target_tag}\" ]\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ deploy_to_peer()\n# Push the tarball, extract on the peer, swap in the new src/bin, record\n# the version. Peer-side runtime setup (serve.sh, OpenRC unit, BIND_IP) is\n# explicitly NOT touched here — that's a separate provisioning concern.\ndeploy_to_peer() {\n    local peer=\"$1\"\n    local tag=\"$2\"\n    local archive_name=\"ollama-${tag}.tar.gz\"\n    local archive_path=\"${DIST_DIR}/${archive_name}\"\n\n    if peer_already_has_version \"${peer}\" \"${tag}\"; then\n        echo \"Peer ${peer} already at ${tag}, skipping.\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n\n    echo \"Deploying ${tag} to ${peer}...\"\n    ssh \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \"mkdir -p ${DIR}\"\n    scp \"${archive_path}\" \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}:${DIR}/\"\n    ssh \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \"\n        set -e\n        cd ${DIR}\n        tar -xzf ${archive_name}\n        rm -rf src bin\n        mv ollama-${tag}/src .\n        mv ollama-${tag}/bin .\n        rmdir ollama-${tag}\n        echo ${tag} > .built-version\n        rm -f ${archive_name}\n    \"\n    echo \"Peer ${peer} updated to ${tag}.\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ main\nmain() {\n    setup_dirs\n    ensure_build_deps\n    bootstrap_go\n\n    local tag\n    tag=\"$(get_latest_tag)\"\n    echo \"Latest upstream release: ${tag}\"\n\n    if already_built \"${tag}\"; then\n        echo \"Local build already at ${tag}, skipping rebuild.\"\n    else\n        fetch_ollama_source \"${tag}\"\n        build_static\n        echo \"${tag}\" > \"${VERSION_FILE}\"\n        echo \"Local build complete: ${tag}\"\n    fi\n\n    package_dist \"${tag}\"\n    deploy_to_peer \"${PEER_1}\" \"${tag}\"\n    deploy_to_peer \"${PEER_2}\" \"${tag}\"\n\n    echo \"All hosts at ${tag}.\"\n}\n# }}}\n\nmain \"$@\"\n",

          "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# ollama-build-and-deploy.sh\n#\n# Bootstrap a fully musl-native, clang-based toolchain on Alpine, then\n# build a fully-static Ollama binary, then ship the source tree and the\n# compiled binary to two peer hosts.\n#\n# Strategy:\n#   stage 0 : install build deps via apk. clang/lld instead of gcc. All\n#             packages are musl-native on Alpine.\n#   stage 1 : bootstrap Go from nothing on musl, compiled with clang:\n#               Go 1.4 (C source) -> Go 1.17.13 -> Go 1.20.14 -> Go 1.22.x\n#             The Alpine-aports musl patchset is applied to Go 1.4 before\n#             building so the ELF interpreter and other glibc-isms are\n#             handled. Every later stage uses the previous one as\n#             GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP. All stages are cached on disk.\n#   stage 2 : ask GitHub for the latest stable Ollama tag. Skip the rebuild\n#             when .built-version matches and the binary already exists.\n#   stage 3 : clone Ollama at that tag. Ollama vendors llama.cpp, and its\n#             Makefile rebuilds the vendored copy via CMake against our\n#             clang toolchain — that's why we get a musl-native llama.cpp\n#             without bootstrapping it separately.\n#   stage 4 : build with full static link flags. Skip per-peer if that peer\n#             already has the same tag recorded.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\n# {{{ config\nDIR=\"${1:-/home/sora/programs/ollama}\"\n\nPEER_1=\"192.168.1.12\"\nPEER_2=\"192.168.1.13\"\nPEER_USER=\"sora\"\n\nBOOTSTRAP_DIR=\"${DIR}/go-bootstrap\"\nGO14_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go1.4\"\nGO17_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go1.17.13\"\nGO20_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go1.20.14\"\nGO_FINAL_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go-final\"\n\nSRC_DIR=\"${DIR}/src\"\nBIN_DIR=\"${DIR}/bin\"\nDIST_DIR=\"${DIR}/dist\"\nLOG_DIR=\"${DIR}/tmp\"\nDOWNLOAD_DIR=\"${DIR}/downloads\"\n\nVERSION_FILE=\"${DIR}/.built-version\"\nOLLAMA_REPO=\"https://github.com/ollama/ollama.git\"\nGITHUB_API=\"https://api.github.com/repos/ollama/ollama/releases/latest\"\n\nGO14_TARBALL=\"go1.4-bootstrap-20171003.tar.gz\"\nGO17_TARBALL=\"go1.17.13.src.tar.gz\"\nGO20_TARBALL=\"go1.20.14.src.tar.gz\"\nGO_FINAL_VERSION=\"1.22.10\"\nGO_FINAL_TARBALL=\"go${GO_FINAL_VERSION}.src.tar.gz\"\n\nGO_DL_BASE=\"https://go.dev/dl\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ setup_dirs()\n# Create the on-disk layout. The log directory is a symlink into /tmp so\n# build noise stays in RAM rather than chewing disk.\nsetup_dirs() {\n    mkdir -p \"${DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${BIN_DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${DIST_DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${DOWNLOAD_DIR}\"\n    if [ ! -L \"${LOG_DIR}\" ]; then\n        local ram_log=\"/tmp/ollama-build-$(id -u)\"\n        mkdir -p \"${ram_log}\"\n        ln -snf \"${ram_log}\" \"${LOG_DIR}\"\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ ensure_build_deps()\n# Pure musl, clang-driven toolchain. No gcc, no build-base, no g++.\n#   clang, clang-dev, lld    -- LLVM C/C++ frontend + linker\n#   compiler-rt              -- LLVM runtime, replaces libgcc\n#   libc++, libc++-dev       -- LLVM C++ standard library (replaces libstdc++)\n#   libunwind, libunwind-dev -- stack-unwinding support libc++abi needs\n#   musl-dev                 -- musl libc headers + static archives\n#   linux-headers            -- kernel uapi headers used by some llama.cpp bits\n#   make, cmake              -- Ollama's Makefile + llama.cpp's CMake build\n#   git, bash, curl          -- plumbing\n#   ca-certificates          -- needed for the GitHub API curl over TLS\nensure_build_deps() {\n    apk add --no-cache \\\n        clang \\\n        clang-dev \\\n        lld \\\n        compiler-rt \\\n        libc++ \\\n        libc++-dev \\\n        libunwind \\\n        libunwind-dev \\\n        musl-dev \\\n        linux-headers \\\n        make \\\n        cmake \\\n        git \\\n        bash \\\n        curl \\\n        ca-certificates\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ download_if_missing()\n# Idempotent download into ${DOWNLOAD_DIR}. Tarballs are kept so retries\n# don't re-fetch, and so a peer can rebuild from the same source artifacts.\ndownload_if_missing() {\n    local filename=\"$1\"\n    local dest=\"${DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${filename}\"\n    if [ -f \"${dest}\" ]; then\n        return 0\n    fi\n    local url=\"${GO_DL_BASE}/${filename}\"\n    echo \"Fetching ${url}\"\n    curl -fsSL \"${url}\" -o \"${dest}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ extract_to()\n# Untar a Go source tarball. Go tarballs always extract a top-level \"go/\"\n# directory; we rename it to the stage-specific install root so all four\n# stages can sit side-by-side.\nextract_to() {\n    local tarball_name=\"$1\"\n    local target_root=\"$2\"\n    local tarball=\"${DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${tarball_name}\"\n    rm -rf \"${target_root}\"\n    local staging\n    staging=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\n    tar -xzf \"${tarball}\" -C \"${staging}\"\n    mv \"${staging}/go\" \"${target_root}\"\n    rmdir \"${staging}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ apply_go14_musl_patches()\n# Patches for Go 1.4 on musl. Replace with musl's actual path.\n#\n#   2. Compiler default. Several places in cmd/dist hardcode \"gcc\" as the\n#      C compiler fallback when CC isn't set. Force \"clang\".\napply_go14_musl_patches() {\n    local root=\"$1\"\n    local f\n\n    # patch 1: ELF interpreter path\n    for f in \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/data.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/lib.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/elf.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/elf.h\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/6l/asm.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/8l/asm.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/5l/asm.c\"\n    do\n        if [ -f \"${f}\" ]; then\n            sed -i 's|/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2|/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1|g' \"${f}\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    # patch 2: replace hardcoded gcc fallback with clang\n    for f in \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/dist/build.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/dist/buildgc.c\"\n    do\n        if [ -f \"${f}\" ]; then\n            sed -i 's|\"gcc\"|\"clang\"|g' \"${f}\"\n        fi\n    done\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ build_go14()\n# Go 1.4 is the last C-based Go. We avoid git\n# ls-remote because it would include drafts and pre-releases.\nget_latest_tag() {\n    local response\n    response=\"$(curl -fsSL \"${GITHUB_API}\")\"\n    local tag\n    tag=\"$(echo \"${response}\" | sed -n 's/.*\"tag_name\": *\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n    if [ -z \"${tag}\" ]; then\n        echo \"ERROR: could not parse latest tag from GitHub API\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    echo \"${tag}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ already_built()\n# Local build is current only if the version file matches AND the binary\n# still exists. Wipes any previous checkout first\n# so stale artifacts from a failed earlier run can't poison the build.\nfetch_ollama_source() {\n    local tag=\"$1\"\n    rm -rf \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n    git clone --depth=1 --branch \"${tag}\" \"${OLLAMA_REPO}\" \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ build_static()\n# Two-phase build of Ollama:\n#\n#   phase A: `make` lets Ollama's Makefile drive CMake for llama.cpp. We\n#            export CC=clang, CXX=clang++, and -stdlib=libc++ flags so the\n#            vendored llama.cpp builds against the LLVM C++ stack rather\n#            than libstdc++. Otherwise we bail out rather than ship a\n# binary that silently depends on libs the peers might not have.\nbuild_static() {\n    cd \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n\n    export CC=clang\n    export CXX=clang++\n    export CGO_ENABLED=1\n    export CGO_CFLAGS=\"-O2\"\n    export CGO_CXXFLAGS=\"-O2 -stdlib=libc++\"\n    export CGO_LDFLAGS=\"-stdlib=libc++ -l:libc++.a -l:libc++abi.a -l:libunwind.a\"\n    export CMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang\n    export CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++\n\n    local makelog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-make.log\"\n    make -j\"$(nproc)\" >\"${makelog}\" 2>&1\n\n    local gobuildlog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-go-build.log\"\n    go build \\\n        -tags 'netgo osusergo' \\\n        -ldflags '-linkmode external -extldflags \"-static -fuse-ld=lld\"' \\\n        -o \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" \\\n        . >\"${gobuildlog}\" 2>&1\n\n    local ldd_out\n    ldd_out=\"$(ldd \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" 2>&1 || true)\"\n    if echo \"${ldd_out}\" | grep -q 'not a dynamic'; then\n        echo \"OK: binary is fully static.\"\n    else\n        echo \"ERROR: binary still has dynamic dependencies:\" >&2\n        echo \"${ldd_out}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ package_dist()\n# Bundle the source tree AND the compiled binary together.     "content":"#!/bin/bash\n# ollama-build-and-deploy.sh\n#\n# Bootstrap a fully musl-native, clang-based toolchain on Alpine, then\n# build a fully-static Ollama binary, then ship the source tree and the\n# compiled binary to two peer hosts.\n#\n# Strategy:\n#   stage 0 : install build deps via apk. clang/lld instead of gcc. All\n#             packages are musl-native on Alpine.\n#   stage 1 : bootstrap Go from nothing on musl, compiled with clang:\n#               Go 1.4 (C source) -> Go 1.17.13 -> Go 1.20.14 -> Go 1.22.x\n#             The Alpine-aports musl patchset is applied to Go 1.4 before\n#             building so the ELF interpreter and other glibc-isms are\n#             handled. Every later stage uses the previous one as\n#             GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP. All stages are cached on disk.\n#   stage 2 : ask GitHub for the latest stable Ollama tag. Skip the rebuild\n#             when .built-version matches and the binary already exists.\n#   stage 3 : clone Ollama at that tag. Ollama vendors llama.cpp, and its\n#             Makefile rebuilds the vendored copy via CMake against our\n#             clang toolchain — that's why we get a musl-native llama.cpp\n#             without bootstrapping it separately.\n#   stage 4 : build with full static link flags. Verify with ldd. Bail\n#             loudly if the binary still has dynamic dependencies.\n#   stage 5 : tar (source tree + binary) into one archive.\n#   stage 6 : scp + extract on two peer hosts. Skip per-peer if that peer\n#             already has the same tag recorded.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\n# {{{ config\nDIR=\"${1:-/home/sora/programs/ollama}\"\n\nPEER_1=\"192.168.1.12\"\nPEER_2=\"192.168.1.13\"\nPEER_USER=\"sora\"\n\nBOOTSTRAP_DIR=\"${DIR}/go-bootstrap\"\nGO14_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go1.4\"\nGO17_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go1.17.13\"\nGO20_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go1.20.14\"\nGO_FINAL_ROOT=\"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}/go-final\"\n\nSRC_DIR=\"${DIR}/src\"\nBIN_DIR=\"${DIR}/bin\"\nDIST_DIR=\"${DIR}/dist\"\nLOG_DIR=\"${DIR}/tmp\"\nDOWNLOAD_DIR=\"${DIR}/downloads\"\n\nVERSION_FILE=\"${DIR}/.built-version\"\nOLLAMA_REPO=\"https://github.com/ollama/ollama.git\"\nGITHUB_API=\"https://api.github.com/repos/ollama/ollama/releases/latest\"\n\nGO14_TARBALL=\"go1.4-bootstrap-20171003.tar.gz\"\nGO17_TARBALL=\"go1.17.13.src.tar.gz\"\nGO20_TARBALL=\"go1.20.14.src.tar.gz\"\nGO_FINAL_VERSION=\"1.22.10\"\nGO_FINAL_TARBALL=\"go${GO_FINAL_VERSION}.src.tar.gz\"\n\nGO_DL_BASE=\"https://go.dev/dl\"\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ setup_dirs()\n# Create the on-disk layout. The log directory is a symlink into /tmp so\n# build noise stays in RAM rather than chewing disk.\nsetup_dirs() {\n    mkdir -p \"${DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${BOOTSTRAP_DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${BIN_DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${DIST_DIR}\"\n    mkdir -p \"${DOWNLOAD_DIR}\"\n    if [ ! -L \"${LOG_DIR}\" ]; then\n        local ram_log=\"/tmp/ollama-build-$(id -u)\"\n        mkdir -p \"${ram_log}\"\n        ln -snf \"${ram_log}\" \"${LOG_DIR}\"\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ ensure_build_deps()\n# Pure musl, clang-driven toolchain. No gcc, no build-base, no g++.\n#   clang, clang-dev, lld    -- LLVM C/C++ frontend + linker\n#   compiler-rt              -- LLVM runtime, replaces libgcc\n#   libc++, libc++-dev       -- LLVM C++ standard library (replaces libstdc++)\n#   libunwind, libunwind-dev -- stack-unwinding support libc++abi needs\n#   musl-dev                 -- musl libc headers + static archives\n#   linux-headers            -- kernel uapi headers used by some llama.cpp bits\n#   make, cmake              -- Ollama's Makefile + llama.cpp's CMake build\n#   git, bash, curl          -- plumbing\n#   ca-certificates          -- needed for the GitHub API curl over TLS\nensure_build_deps() {\n    apk add --no-cache \\\n        clang \\\n        clang-dev \\\n        lld \\\n        compiler-rt \\\n        libc++ \\\n        libc++-dev \\\n        libunwind \\\n        libunwind-dev \\\n        musl-dev \\\n        linux-headers \\\n        make \\\n        cmake \\\n        git \\\n        bash \\\n        curl \\\n        ca-certificates\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ download_if_missing()\n# Idempotent download into ${DOWNLOAD_DIR}. Tarballs are kept so retries\n# don't re-fetch, and so a peer can rebuild from the same source artifacts.\ndownload_if_missing() {\n    local filename=\"$1\"\n    local dest=\"${DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${filename}\"\n    if [ -f \"${dest}\" ]; then\n        return 0\n    fi\n    local url=\"${GO_DL_BASE}/${filename}\"\n    echo \"Fetching ${url}\"\n    curl -fsSL \"${url}\" -o \"${dest}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ extract_to()\n# Untar a Go source tarball. Go tarballs always extract a top-level \"go/\"\n# directory; we rename it to the stage-specific install root so all four\n# stages can sit side-by-side.\nextract_to() {\n    local tarball_name=\"$1\"\n    local target_root=\"$2\"\n    local tarball=\"${DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${tarball_name}\"\n    rm -rf \"${target_root}\"\n    local staging\n    staging=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\n    tar -xzf \"${tarball}\" -C \"${staging}\"\n    mv \"${staging}/go\" \"${target_root}\"\n    rmdir \"${staging}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ apply_go14_musl_patches()\n# Patches for Go 1.4 on musl. These are the canonical edits Alpine has\n# carried in its historical go-bootstrap aport. They are applied\n# unconditionally — when a target file is missing on this Go 1.4 variant\n# the patch loop just skips it, but every patch that does apply is\n# necessary and documented.\n#\n#   1. Glibc dynamic linker path. Go 1.4's linker hard-codes\n#      \"/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2\" as the ELF program interpreter,\n#      which doesn't exist on musl. Replace with musl's actual path.\n#\n#   2. Compiler default. Several places in cmd/dist hardcode \"gcc\" as the\n#      C compiler fallback when CC isn't set. Force \"clang\".\napply_go14_musl_patches() {\n    local root=\"$1\"\n    local f\n\n    # patch 1: ELF interpreter path\n    for f in \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/data.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/lib.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/elf.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/elf.h\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/6l/asm.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/8l/asm.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/5l/asm.c\"\n    do\n        if [ -f \"${f}\" ]; then\n            sed -i 's|/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2|/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1|g' \"${f}\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    # patch 2: replace hardcoded gcc fallback with clang\n    for f in \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/dist/build.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/dist/buildgc.c\"\n    do\n        if [ -f \"${f}\" ]; then\n            sed -i 's|\"gcc\"|\"clang\"|g' \"${f}\"\n        fi\n    done\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ build_go14()\n# Go 1.4 is the last C-based Go. CGO_ENABLED=0 keeps it from probing for\n# a libc toolchain layout it wouldn't recognize on Alpine. We set CC=clang\n# explicitly so make.bash doesn't go looking for gcc.\nbuild_go14() {\n    if [ -x \"${GO14_ROOT}/bin/go\" ]; then\n        echo \"Go 1.4 already built, skipping.\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    echo \"Bootstrap stage 1/4: building Go 1.4 from C source\"\n    download_if_missing \"${GO14_TARBALL}\"\n    extract_to \"${GO14_TARBALL}\" \"${GO14_ROOT}\"\n    apply_go14_musl_patches \"${GO14_ROOT}\"\n\n    local build_log=\"${LOG_DIR}/go1.4-build.log\"\n    (\n        cd \"${GO14_ROOT}/src\"\n        export CC=clang\n        export CGO_ENABLED=0\n        ./make.bash --no-clean\n    ) >\"${build_log}\" 2>&1\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ build_go_stage()\n# Generic stage builder for Go 1.5+: every later Go version requires the\n# previous one as GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP. We pass CC=clang so the runtime's C\n# bits build with the same compiler as everything else.\nbuild_go_stage() {\n    local stage_name=\"$1\"\n    local tarball_name=\"$2\"\n    local target_root=\"$3\"\n    local bootstrap_root=\"$4\"\n\n    if [ -x \"${target_root}/bin/go\" ]; then\n        echo \"${stage_name} already built, skipping.\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n    echo \"Bootstrap ${stage_name}: building ${tarball_name}\"\n    download_if_missing \"${tarball_name}\"\n    extract_to \"${tarball_name}\" \"${target_root}\"\n\n    local build_log=\"${LOG_DIR}/${stage_name}-build.log\"\n    (\n        cd \"${target_root}/src\"\n        export CC=clang\n        export CXX=clang++\n        export GOROOT_BOOTSTRAP=\"${bootstrap_root}\"\n        export CGO_ENABLED=1\n        ./make.bash\n    ) >\"${build_log}\" 2>&1\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ bootstrap_go()\n# Full Go bootstrap chain. Each stage is idempotent — built once, cached\n# on disk, skipped on subsequent runs.\nbootstrap_go() {\n    build_go14\n    build_go_stage \"go1.17.13\" \"${GO17_TARBALL}\" \"${GO17_ROOT}\" \"${GO14_ROOT}\"\n    build_go_stage \"go1.20.14\" \"${GO20_TARBALL}\" \"${GO20_ROOT}\" \"${GO17_ROOT}\"\n    build_go_stage \"go${GO_FINAL_VERSION}\" \"${GO_FINAL_TARBALL}\" \"${GO_FINAL_ROOT}\" \"${GO20_ROOT}\"\n\n    export GOROOT=\"${GO_FINAL_ROOT}\"\n    export PATH=\"${GO_FINAL_ROOT}/bin:${PATH}\"\n    echo \"Go ready: $(go version)\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ get_latest_tag()\n# Ask GitHub for the most recent published release tag. We avoid git\n# ls-remote because it would include drafts and pre-releases.\nget_latest_tag() {\n    local response\n    response=\"$(curl -fsSL \"${GITHUB_API}\")\"\n    local tag\n    tag=\"$(echo \"${response}\" | sed -n 's/.*\"tag_name\": *\"\\([^\"]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' | head -n1)\"\n    if [ -z \"${tag}\" ]; then\n        echo \"ERROR: could not parse latest tag from GitHub API\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    echo \"${tag}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ already_built()\n# Local build is current only if the version file matches AND the binary\n# still exists. Either failing forces a rebuild.\nalready_built() {\n    local target_tag=\"$1\"\n    if [ ! -f \"${VERSION_FILE}\" ]; then\n        return 1\n    fi\n    if [ ! -x \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" ]; then\n        return 1\n    fi\n    local built_tag\n    built_tag=\"$(cat \"${VERSION_FILE}\")\"\n    [ \"${built_tag}\" = \"${target_tag}\" ]\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ fetch_ollama_source()\n# Shallow clone of the tagged release. Wipes any previous checkout first\n# so stale artifacts from a failed earlier run can't poison the build.\nfetch_ollama_source() {\n    local tag=\"$1\"\n    rm -rf \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n    git clone --depth=1 --branch \"${tag}\" \"${OLLAMA_REPO}\" \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ build_static()\n# Two-phase build of Ollama:\n#\n#   phase A: `make` lets Ollama's Makefile drive CMake for llama.cpp. We\n#            export CC=clang, CXX=clang++, and -stdlib=libc++ flags so the\n#            vendored llama.cpp builds against the LLVM C++ stack rather\n#            than libstdc++. CGO_LDFLAGS pre-loads the static linkage of\n#            libc++/libc++abi/libunwind for the cgo step.\n#\n#   phase B: rebuild the Go binary explicitly with -linkmode external and\n#            -extldflags '-static'. Ollama's Makefile invokes go build\n#            without these flags, so we redo that step ourselves.\n#\n# The ldd check at the end is non-negotiable: the binary must be reported\n# as \"not a dynamic executable\". Otherwise we bail out rather than ship a\n# binary that silently depends on libs the peers might not have.\nbuild_static() {\n    cd \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n\n    export CC=clang\n    export CXX=clang++\n    export CGO_ENABLED=1\n    export CGO_CFLAGS=\"-O2\"\n    export CGO_CXXFLAGS=\"-O2 -stdlib=libc++\"\n    export CGO_LDFLAGS=\"-stdlib=libc++ -l:libc++.a -l:libc++abi.a -l:libunwind.a\"\n    export CMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang\n    export CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++\n\n    local makelog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-make.log\"\n    make -j\"$(nproc)\" >\"${makelog}\" 2>&1\n\n    local gobuildlog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-go-build.log\"\n    go build \\\n        -tags 'netgo osusergo' \\\n        -ldflags '-linkmode external -extldflags \"-static -fuse-ld=lld\"' \\\n        -o \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" \\\n        . >\"${gobuildlog}\" 2>&1\n\n    local ldd_out\n    ldd_out=\"$(ldd \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" 2>&1 || true)\"\n    if echo \"${ldd_out}\" | grep -q 'not a dynamic'; then\n        echo \"OK: binary is fully static.\"\n    else\n        echo \"ERROR: binary still has dynamic dependencies:\" >&2\n        echo \"${ldd_out}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ package_dist()\n# Bundle the source tree AND the compiled binary together. Peers receive\n# both so they can either run as-is or rebuild from source themselves.\npackage_dist() {\n    local tag=\"$1\"\n    local archive_name=\"ollama-${tag}.tar.gz\"\n    local archive_path=\"${DIST_DIR}/${archive_name}\"\n    rm -f \"${archive_path}\"\n    tar -czf \"${archive_path}\" \\\n        -C \"${DIR}\" \\\n        --transform \"s,^src,ollama-${tag}/src,\" \\\n        --transform \"s,^bin,ollama-${tag}/bin,\" \\\n        src bin\n    echo \"Packaged: ${archive_path}\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ peer_already_has_version()\n# Cheap remote check so we don't re-scp when the peer is already current.\n# Network or ssh failure is treated as \"not current\" — better to over-deploy\n# than to skip a peer that's actually out of date.\npeer_already_has_version() {\n    local peer=\"$1\"\n    local target_tag=\"$2\"\n    local peer_version\n    peer_version=\"$(ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \\\n        \"cat ${DIR}/.built-version 2>/dev/null || echo none\" 2>/dev/null || echo none)\"\n    [ \"${peer_version}\" = \"${target_tag}\" ]\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ deploy_to_peer()\n# Push the tarball, extract on the peer, swap in the new src/bin, record\n# the version. Runtime setup (serve.sh, OpenRC unit, BIND_IP) on the peer\n# is explicitly NOT touched — that's a separate provisioning concern.\ndeploy_to_peer() {\n    local peer=\"$1\"\n    local tag=\"$2\"\n    local archive_name=\"ollama-${tag}.tar.gz\"\n    local archive_path=\"${DIST_DIR}/${archive_name}\"\n\n    if peer_already_has_version \"${peer}\" \"${tag}\"; then\n        echo \"Peer ${peer} already at ${tag}, skipping.\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n\n    echo \"Deploying ${tag} to ${peer}...\"\n    ssh \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \"mkdir -p ${DIR}\"\n    scp \"${archive_path}\" \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}:${DIR}/\"\n    ssh \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \"\n        set -e\n        cd ${DIR}\n        tar -xzf ${archive_name}\n        rm -rf src bin\n        mv ollama-${tag}/src .\n        mv ollama-${tag}/bin .\n        rmdir ollama-${tag}\n        echo ${tag} > .built-version\n        rm -f ${archive_name}\n    \"\n    echo \"Peer ${peer} updated to ${tag}.\"\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ main\nmain() {\n    setup_dirs\n    ensure_build_deps\n    bootstrap_go\n\n    local tag\n    tag=\"$(get_latest_tag)\"\n    echo \"Latest upstream release: ${tag}\"\n\n    if already_built \"${tag}\"; then\n        echo \"Local build already at ${tag}, skipping rebuild.\"\n    else\n        fetch_ollama_source \"${tag}\"\n        build_static\n        echo \"${tag}\" > \"${VERSION_FILE}\"\n        echo \"Local build complete: ${tag}\"\n    fi\n\n    package_dist \"${tag}\"\n    deploy_to_peer \"${PEER_1}\" \"${tag}\"\n    deploy_to_peer \"${PEER_2}\" \"${tag}\"\n\n    echo \"All hosts at ${tag}.\"\n}\n# }}}\n\nmain \"$@\"\n",
    "filePath":"/tmp/ollama-build-and-deploy.sh"
  },

Since we hand it `CC=clang CXX=clang++` with libc++ flags, that vendored llama.cpp compiles against musl from scratch. They are applied\n# unconditionally — when a target file is missing on this Go 1.4 variant\n# the patch loop just skips it, but every patch that does apply is\n# necessary and documented.\n#\n#   1. Glibc dynamic linker path. Go 1.4's linker hard-codes\n#      \"/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2\" as the ELF program interpreter,\n#      which doesn't exist on musl. Replace with musl's actual path.\n#\n#   2. Compiler default. Several places in cmd/dist hardcode \"gcc\" as the\n#      C compiler fallback when CC isn't set. Force \"clang\".\napply_go14_musl_patches() {\n    local root=\"$1\"\n    local f\n\n    # patch 1: ELF interpreter path\n    for f in \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/data.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/lib.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/elf.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/ld/elf.h\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/6l/asm.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/8l/asm.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/5l/asm.c\"\n    do\n        if [ -f \"${f}\" ]; then\n            sed -i 's|/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2|/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1|g' \"${f}\"\n        fi\n    done\n\n    # patch 2: replace hardcoded gcc fallback with clang\n    for f in \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/dist/build.c\" \\\n        \"${root}/src/cmd/dist/buildgc.c\"\n    do\n        if [ -f \"${f}\" ]; then\n            sed -i 's|\"gcc\"|\"clang\"|g' \"${f}\"\n        fi\n    done\n}\n# }}}"

          "new_string":"# {{{ build_static()\n# Two-phase build of Ollama:\n#\n#   phase A: `make` lets Ollama's Makefile drive CMake for llama.cpp. The\n#            vendored llama.cpp gets compiled from scratch against gcc/g++\n#            from build-base, which on Alpine is musl-linked. CGO_LDFLAGS\n#            pre-loads the static-C++-runtime flags so the cgo link step\n#            doesn't leave libstdc++/libgcc as dynamic deps.\n#\n#   phase B: rebuild the Go binary explicitly with -linkmode external and\n#            -extldflags '-static'. Ollama's Makefile invokes go build\n#            without these flags, so we redo that step ourselves.\n#\n# The ldd check at the end is non-negotiable: the binary must be reported\n# as \"not a dynamic executable\". Otherwise we bail out rather than ship a\n# binary that silently depends on libs the peers might not have.\nbuild_static() {\n    cd \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n\n    export CGO_ENABLED=1\n    export CC=gcc\n    export CXX=g++\n    export CGO_CFLAGS=\"-O2\"\n    export CGO_CXXFLAGS=\"-O2\"\n    export CGO_LDFLAGS=\"-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc\"\n\n    local makelog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-make.log\"\n    make -j\"$(nproc)\" >\"${makelog}\" 2>&1\n\n    local gobuildlog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-go-build.log\"\n    go build \\\n        -tags 'netgo osusergo' \\\n        -ldflags '-linkmode external -extldflags \"-static\"' \\\n        -o \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" \\\n        . >\"${gobuildlog}\" 2>&1\n\n    local ldd_out\n    ldd_out=\"$(ldd \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" 2>&1 || true)\"\n    if echo \"${ldd_out}\" | grep -q 'not a dynamic'; then\n        echo \"OK: binary is fully static.\"\n    else\n        echo \"ERROR: binary still has dynamic dependencies:\" >&2\n        echo \"${ldd_out}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n}\n# }}}",
          "old_string":"# {{{ build_static()\n# Two-phase build of Ollama:\n#\n#   phase A: `make` lets Ollama's Makefile drive CMake for llama.cpp. We\n#            export CC=clang, CXX=clang++, and -stdlib=libc++ flags so the\n#            vendored llama.cpp builds against the LLVM C++ stack rather\n#            than libstdc++. CGO_LDFLAGS pre-loads the static linkage of\n#            libc++/libc++abi/libunwind for the cgo step.\n#\n#   phase B: rebuild the Go binary explicitly with -linkmode external and\n#            -extldflags '-static'. Ollama's Makefile invokes go build\n#            without these flags, so we redo that step ourselves.\n#\n# The ldd check at the end is non-negotiable: the binary must be reported\n# as \"not a dynamic executable\". Otherwise we bail out rather than ship a\n# binary that silently depends on libs the peers might not have.\nbuild_static() {\n    cd \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n\n    export CC=clang\n    export CXX=clang++\n    export CGO_ENABLED=1\n    export CGO_CFLAGS=\"-O2\"\n    export CGO_CXXFLAGS=\"-O2 -stdlib=libc++\"\n    export CGO_LDFLAGS=\"-stdlib=libc++ -l:libc++.a -l:libc++abi.a -l:libunwind.a\"\n    export CMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang\n    export CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++\n\n    local makelog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-make.log\"\n    make -j\"$(nproc)\" >\"${makelog}\" 2>&1\n\n    local gobuildlog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-go-build.log\"\n    go build \\\n        -tags 'netgo osusergo' \\\n        -ldflags '-linkmode external -extldflags \"-static -fuse-ld=lld\"' \\\n        -o \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" \\\n        . >\"${gobuildlog}\" 2>&1\n\n    local ldd_out\n    ldd_out=\"$(ldd \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" 2>&1 || true)\"\n    if echo \"${ldd_out}\" | grep -q 'not a dynamic'; then\n        echo \"OK: binary is fully static.\"\n    else\n        echo \"ERROR: binary still has dynamic dependencies:\" >&2\n        echo \"${ldd_out}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n}\n# }}}"

CGO_LDFLAGS pre-loads the static linkage of","-#            libc++/libc++abi/libunwind for the cgo step.","+#   phase A: `make` lets Ollama's Makefile drive CMake for llama.cpp. The","+#            vendored llama.cpp gets compiled from scratch against gcc/g++","+#            from build-base, which on Alpine is musl-linked. CGO_LDFLAGS","+#            pre-loads the static-C++-runtime flags so the cgo link step","+#            doesn't leave libstdc++/libgcc as dynamic deps."," #"," #   phase B: rebuild the Go binary explicitly with -linkmode external and"," #            -extldflags '-static'. Ollama's Makefile invokes go build"]

        "lines":[" build_static() {","     cd \"${SRC_DIR}\""," ","-    export CC=clang","-    export CXX=clang++","     export CGO_ENABLED=1","+    export CC=gcc","+    export CXX=g++","     export CGO_CFLAGS=\"-O2\"","-    export CGO_CXXFLAGS=\"-O2 -stdlib=libc++\"","-    export CGO_LDFLAGS=\"-stdlib=libc++ -l:libc++.a -l:libc++abi.a -l:libunwind.a\"","-    export CMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang","-    export CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++","+    export CGO_CXXFLAGS=\"-O2\"","+    export CGO_LDFLAGS=\"-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc\""," ","     local makelog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-make.log\"","     make -j\"$(nproc)\" >\"${makelog}\" 2>&1"]

    "oldString":"# {{{ build_static()\n# Two-phase build of Ollama:\n#\n#   phase A: `make` lets Ollama's Makefile drive CMake for llama.cpp. We\n#            export CC=clang, CXX=clang++, and -stdlib=libc++ flags so the\n#            vendored llama.cpp builds against the LLVM C++ stack rather\n#            than libstdc++. CGO_LDFLAGS pre-loads the static linkage of\n#            libc++/libc++abi/libunwind for the cgo step.\n#\n#   phase B: rebuild the Go binary explicitly with -linkmode external and\n#            -extldflags '-static'. Ollama's Makefile invokes go build\n#            without these flags, so we redo that step ourselves.\n#\n# The ldd check at the end is non-negotiable: the binary must be reported\n# as \"not a dynamic executable\". Otherwise we bail out rather than ship a\n# binary that silently depends on libs the peers might not have.\nbuild_static() {\n    cd \"${SRC_DIR}\"\n\n    export CC=clang\n    export CXX=clang++\n    export CGO_ENABLED=1\n    export CGO_CFLAGS=\"-O2\"\n    export CGO_CXXFLAGS=\"-O2 -stdlib=libc++\"\n    export CGO_LDFLAGS=\"-stdlib=libc++ -l:libc++.a -l:libc++abi.a -l:libunwind.a\"\n    export CMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang\n    export CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++\n\n    local makelog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-make.log\"\n    make -j\"$(nproc)\" >\"${makelog}\" 2>&1\n\n    local gobuildlog=\"${LOG_DIR}/ollama-go-build.log\"\n    go build \\\n        -tags 'netgo osusergo' \\\n        -ldflags '-linkmode external -extldflags \"-static -fuse-ld=lld\"' \\\n        -o \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" \\\n        . >\"${gobuildlog}\" 2>&1\n\n    local ldd_out\n    ldd_out=\"$(ldd \"${BIN_DIR}/ollama\" 2>&1 || true)\"\n    if echo \"${ldd_out}\" | grep -q 'not a dynamic'; then\n        echo \"OK: binary is fully static.\"\n    else\n        echo \"ERROR: binary still has dynamic dependencies:\" >&2\n        echo \"${ldd_out}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n}\n# }}}",
    "filePath":"/tmp/ollama-build-and-deploy.sh"
  },

        "type":"text",
        "text":"Classic Alpine gotcha. Two likely causes:\n\n**1. `bash` isn't installed yet.** Alpine ships with `ash` (busybox), not bash. The shebang `#!/bin/bash` resolves to a nonexistent file, and the kernel reports that as \"not found\" on the script itself rather than on the interpreter — which is confusing.\n\n```\napk add bash\n./ollama-build-and-deploy.sh\n```\n\nThe script itself installs bash in `ensure_build_deps()`, but it can't get there if the shell can't load it in the first place. Chicken-and-egg. One-time `apk add bash` fixes it.\n\n**2. CRLF line endings**, if the script took a Windows detour somewhere. Check with:\n\n```\nhead -1 ollama-build-and-deploy.sh | od -c | head -1\n```\n\nIf you see `\\r \\n` at the end of the shebang instead of just `\\n`, that's the issue. Fix:\n\n```\nsed -i 's/\\r$//' ollama-build-and-deploy.sh\n```\n\nVerify also that the file actually has execute permission:\n\n```\nls -la ollama-build-and-deploy.sh\n```\n\nIf the mode column doesn't show `x`, `chmod +x ollama-build-and-deploy.sh`.\n\nMy bet is #1 — `apk add bash` and you're moving."
      }]
  },

The script doesn't use anything bash-specific — I scanned it for `[[ ]]`, `<( )`, herestrings, `BASH_*` vars, `function` keyword, brace-range expansion, `mapfile` — none of it.\n\n## ash vs bash, briefly\n\n`ash` (in Alpine, it's busybox's ash) is the small POSIX-focused shell. bash is GNU's larger one with a lot of extensions. The differences that matter for a script like ours:\n\n| feature | bash | busybox ash |\n|---|---|---|\n| `[[ ... ]]` test | yes | no — use `[ ... ]` |\n| arrays | yes | no |\n| `<(cmd)` process substitution | yes | no |\n| `<<<` herestring | yes | no |\n| `{a,b,c}` brace expansion | yes | no |\n| `local` in functions | yes | yes (extension) |\n| `set -o pipefail` | yes | yes (since busybox 1.30) |\n| `$(...)` command substitution | yes | yes |\n| `${var:-default}` parameter expansion | yes | yes |\n| heredocs | yes | yes |\n| `function name() {` | yes | no — use `name() {` |\n| `echo -e` | yes (sort of) | yes |\n\nWe only use the things in the \"both support\" rows. Specifically:\n- `local var=...` inside functions\n- `$(command)` substitution\n- `${var:-default}` expansion\n- `[ ... ]` tests (POSIX-style, never `[[`)\n- `name() { ... }` function syntax (never `function`)\n- `set -euo pipefail` (busybox ash supports `pipefail`)\n- subshells via `( ... )`\n- `for` and `if` (POSIX forms)\n- heredocs inside the SSH deploy step\n\nAll of that runs under `/bin/sh` on Alpine without modification.\n\n## Change to make\n\nTwo lines. First, swap the shebang:"

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Changes in this revision:\n\n1. **`download_if_missing()`** now downloads to `${dest}.partial` and renames on success. If curl is interrupted, the partial file stays as `.partial` and the next run re-downloads instead of trusting a corrupt cache. Also prints \"Already cached\" when skipping, so silent steps are no longer invisible.\n\n2. **Every compile step** (`build_go14`, `build_go_stage`, `build_static`) now wraps its log redirection in an `if ! ...; then tail -n 100; exit 1; fi` pattern. When a build fails, the last 100 lines of the log get dumped to stderr automatically. You'll see the actual compiler error inline instead of a silent exit.\n\n3. **Modern-gcc compatibility flags for Go 1.4**, embedded into `CC`:\n   `-fcommon -Wno-error -Wno-implicit-function-declaration -Wno-implicit-int -Wno-int-conversion -Wno-return-type -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types -Wno-unused-result`\n\n   These suppress the errors gcc 15.2 would raise on Go 1.4's 2014-era C source — implicit declarations, missing return types, int-to-pointer conversions. They only affect Go 1.4's bootstrap build; the later Go stages don't need them since they've been kept compatible with modern compilers.\n\n4. **Step markers** between silent operations. Each phase now prints what it's about to do, so a hang or silent failure narrows to a specific step instead of \"somewhere in the script.\"\n\n## Before re-running\n\nThere's likely a partial `go1.4-bootstrap-20171003.tar.gz` from the previous attempt sitting in `/home/sora/programs/ollama/downloads/`. The new download logic won't detect that as partial (it doesn't have the `.partial` suffix because it was written by the old code). Worth nuking it once so the script can do a clean fetch:\n\n```\nrm -f /home/sora/programs/ollama/downloads/go1.4-bootstrap-20171003.tar.gz\n```\n\nThen re-copy `/tmp/ollama-build-and-deploy.sh` to the host and run again. If anything fails, you'll see the actual error in the output now."

          "new_string":"# {{{ build_static()\n# Ollama's build flow at recent tags:\n#\n#   phase A (optional): if a top-level Makefile exists, run it. Older tags\n#            (pre-v0.4 or so) used a Makefile to drive CMake for llama.cpp.\n#            v0.24.0 and similar don't have one — llama.cpp builds via\n#            cgo directly.\n#\n#   phase B: `go generate ./...` runs whatever generators the source tree\n#            registers — typically code-gen for the vendored llama.cpp\n#            cgo bindings.\n#\n#   phase C: `go build` with full static link flags. -linkmode external\n#            forces the system linker (which handles C++ symbols) and\n#            -extldflags '-static' pulls in musl and the C++ runtime\n#            statically.         "type":"text",
        "text":"Three branches now:\n\n1. **No `.git` directory** → shallow clone at the target tag (the only case that hits the full clone path).\n2. **`.git` exists, tag matches** → leave the tree alone, save the bandwidth and the time.\n3. **`.git` exists, different tag** → `git fetch --depth=1` just the new tag, `git reset --hard` to it, `git clean -fdx` to wipe any build artifacts that linger from the previous tag.\n\nThe `--depth=1` fetch keeps it cheap even when switching tags — only the new commit is pulled, no full history.\n\nOne side effect to be aware of: the `git clean -fdx` in the tag-switch path also removes anything in `${SRC_DIR}` that isn't tracked by git. That includes any local edits to the source tree. For our use case (clean build host, no manual edits) that's the right behavior; if anyone ever wants to hack on the Ollama source in place, they'd need to do it outside `${SRC_DIR}` or stash before re-running.\n\nRe-copy and run."
      }]
  },

Naturally terse, strong factual recall, reasonable reasoning. Pull command: `ollama pull qwen2.5:3b` |\n| **phi3.5:3.8b** | ~2.2 GB | ~3.5 GB | Microsoft's reasoning-focused model. Excellent precision-per-token; if you ask it a math/logic/factual question it'll usually get there in fewer wandering tokens than a Llama variant. `ollama pull phi3.5` |\n| **llama3.2:3b** | ~2.0 GB | ~3 GB | Meta's. Better general world-knowledge breadth than Qwen, slightly worse at being concise. `ollama pull llama3.2:3b` |\n| **qwen2.5:1.5b** | ~1.0 GB | ~1.5 GB | Speed pick. Surprisingly capable for size — useful if 3B-class is too slow. `ollama pull qwen2.5:1.5b` |\n| **gemma2:2b** | ~1.6 GB | ~2 GB | Google's; solid multilingual, otherwise unexceptional. State uncertainty plainly.\"* and it'll behave.\n\nOne sanity check before you pull anything: how much RAM do the sora hosts actually have? On Alpine, `free -h` will tell you.         "type":"text",
        "text":"Short answer: **all of it can go in the script.** Specifically:\n\n1. **`serve.sh` per host** — write the launcher with the right `BIND_IP` for each host. No root needed (lives in `/home/sora/programs/ollama/`).\n2. **`/etc/init.d/ollama` OpenRC unit** — generate and install. Needs root.\n3. **`rc-update add ollama default`** — enable on boot. Needs root.\n4. **`rc-service ollama restart`** — restart after a binary update. Needs root.\n\nThe script already runs as root locally, so on the build host all four are trivial. The constraint is on **peers**: the deploy step ssh's in as `sora`, who can't write `/etc/init.d/` or invoke `rc-service`. So the question reduces to: how do we get privileged operations on each peer?\n\nThree ways, in order of recommendation:\n\n**1. doas with a narrow rule (recommended).** One-time config on each peer:\n\n```\necho \"permit nopass sora as root cmd /sbin/rc-service\" >> /etc/doas.d/doas.conf\necho \"permit nopass sora as root cmd /sbin/rc-update\" >> /etc/doas.d/doas.conf\necho \"permit nopass sora as root cmd /bin/mv args /tmp/ollama-init /etc/init.d/ollama\" >> /etc/doas.d/doas.conf\n```\n\nThen the script ssh's as `sora` and prefixes the privileged calls with `doas`. Tight scope, no full-root ssh.\n\n**2. SSH as root.** Add `PEER_USER_ROOT=\"root\"` config var, ssh-copy-id once to `root@peer1`/`peer2`. Simpler but gives a key full-root access to each peer forever.\n\n**3. Drop a `finalize.sh` on each peer, run it once manually as root.** Service setup happens one time; subsequent binary updates after re-builds wouldn't auto-restart (you'd `rc-service ollama restart` by hand or accept that systemd-style auto-restart isn't happening).\n\n## What I'd recommend including\n\nA `provision_runtime` step that runs after the binary deploy and does, per host:\n\n- Write `${DIR}/serve.sh` with the correct `BIND_IP` for that host (= the IP we just ssh'd to, or for the local host, a `LOCAL_BIND_IP` config var).\n- Write `/etc/init.d/ollama` from a heredoc in the script.\n- `rc-update add ollama default` (idempotent, won't double-add).\n- `rc-service ollama restart` (handles both \"first start\" and \"restart after binary update\").\n\nWith doas configured, that whole block is automatable end-to-end. The script becomes one-stop: \"I am the build host, here are my peers, run me and everything ends up serving.\"\n\nWant me to add it? If so, do you want the doas path or the root-ssh path? Doas is cleaner from a security-of-key-material standpoint; root-ssh is one less moving part."
      }]
  },

The unit is identical\n# across hosts — only serve.sh differs per host.\nemit_openrc_unit() {\n    cat <<EOF\n#!/sbin/openrc-run\n# Ollama service unit. Installed by ollama-build-and-deploy.sh.\n\nname=\"ollama\"\ndescription=\"Ollama LLM server\"\n\ncommand=\"${DIR}/serve.sh\"\ncommand_user=\"${PEER_USER}:${PEER_USER}\"\ncommand_background=true\npidfile=\"/run/ollama.pid\"\noutput_log=\"/var/log/ollama.log\"\nerror_log=\"/var/log/ollama.log\"\n\ndepend() {\n    need net\n    after firewall\n}\nEOF\n}\n# }}}\n\n# {{{ provision_local()\n# Set up the runtime on the build host itself.     "id":"msg_01BY3pkJY4b4F9xbTbMcZnRy",
    "role":"assistant",
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"## What was added\n\n**Config (top of script):**\n- `OLLAMA_PORT=\"10000\"` — shared across all hosts.\n- `LOCAL_BIND_IP=\"\"` — auto-detected from the routing table if empty; override here if needed.\n- `MODELS_DIR=\"${DIR}/models\"` — pulled-model storage.\n\n**Five new functions:**\n- `detect_local_ip` — uses `ip route get 1.1.1.1` to find the IP the kernel would use for outbound traffic. That's the same IP the host should advertise.\n- `emit_serve_sh` — generates the launcher with the right `BIND_IP` baked in.\n- `emit_openrc_unit` — generates `/etc/init.d/ollama` (identical across hosts, only differs by what `serve.sh` it invokes).\n- `provision_local` — runs the install/enable/restart locally (we're already root).\n- `provision_peer` — stages files via scp, then runs the privileged ops via doas in a single ssh session.\n\n**`main` extended** to run the three provision steps after the binary deploy. Idempotent end-to-end — re-running the whole script on a host that's already provisioned just refreshes the files and restarts the service.\n\n## One-time doas setup per peer\n\nThe script needs three doas rules in place before the peer step works. On each peer (`sora2`, `sora3`), as root, once:\n\n```\ncat >> /etc/doas.d/doas.conf <<'EOF'\npermit nopass sora cmd /usr/bin/install\npermit nopass sora cmd /sbin/rc-update args add ollama default\npermit nopass sora cmd /sbin/rc-service args ollama restart\nEOF\n```\n\nAfter that, all subsequent `./ollama-build-and-deploy.sh` runs from the build host fully provision the peers without interactive prompts.\n\n## What happens on the next run\n\nOn the build host (sora1):\n1. Goes through all the cached stages (Go bootstrap, source, build) — nothing rebuilds.\n2. Packages the existing binary into a tarball.\n3. Skips per-peer deploy because both peers report v0.24.0 already.\n4. **New**: provisions local runtime → writes `serve.sh`, installs `/etc/init.d/ollama`, enables on boot, starts the service.\n5. **New**: provisions each peer the same way over ssh + doas.\n\nRe-copy `/tmp/ollama-build-and-deploy.sh`, add the doas rules on the peers, and run. Listen check after:\n\n```\ncurl http://192.168.1.11:10000/api/tags\n```\n\nThat'll be the moment of truth — should return `{\"models\":[]}` from each of the three hosts on their respective IP:port."
      }]
  },

We are already root, so no\n# extra privilege escalation needed; just write files and invoke OpenRC\n# directly. Idempotent: serve.sh and the unit are overwritten in place,\n# rc-update doesn't fail on already-added services, rc-service restart\n# works whether the service is running or not.\nprovision_local() {\n    local bind_ip=\"$1\"\n    local port=\"$2\"\n    echo \"Provisioning local runtime (bind ${bind_ip}:${port})...\"\n\n    emit_serve_sh \"${bind_ip}\" \"${port}\" > \"${DIR}/serve.sh\"\n    chmod +x \"${DIR}/serve.sh\"\n    chown \"${PEER_USER}:${PEER_USER}\" \"${DIR}/serve.sh\"\n\n    mkdir -p \"${MODELS_DIR}\"\n    chown -R \"${PEER_USER}:${PEER_USER}\" \"${MODELS_DIR}\"\n\n    emit_openrc_unit > /etc/init.d/ollama\n    chmod +x /etc/init.d/ollama\n    chown root:root /etc/init.d/ollama\n\n    rc-update add ollama default 2>/dev/null || true\n    rc-service ollama restart\n    echo \"Local runtime ready.\"\n}\n# }}}",

          "new_string":"# {{{ provision_peer()\n# Set up the runtime on a peer over ssh, using two identities:\n#\n#   - PEER_USER (sora) for everything under /home/sora/programs/ollama/.\n#     serve.sh and the models directory live there.\n#   - PEER_ROOT (root) for /etc/init.d/ollama and the rc-update /\n#     rc-service calls.\n#\n# The bind IP for the peer is the same as the ssh address: each peer binds\n# its own publicly-reachable IP. The port is per-host from port_for_ip.\n# Generated serve.sh is unique to this peer's IP+port, so a mis-copy to\n# the wrong host would be immediately obvious (wrong port, wrong IP).\nprovision_peer() {\n    local peer=\"$1\"\n    local port=\"$2\"\n    echo \"Provisioning ${peer} (bind ${peer}:${port})...\"\n\n    local tmp_serve\n    tmp_serve=\"$(mktemp)\"\n    emit_serve_sh \"${peer}\" \"${port}\" > \"${tmp_serve}\"\n\n    local tmp_init\n    tmp_init=\"$(mktemp)\"\n    emit_openrc_unit > \"${tmp_init}\"\n\n    # serve.sh + models dir: unprivileged\n    scp -q \"${tmp_serve}\" \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}:${DIR}/serve.sh\"\n    ssh \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \"\n        set -e\n        chmod +x ${DIR}/serve.sh\n        mkdir -p ${MODELS_DIR}\n    \"\n\n    # OpenRC unit + service ops: privileged\n    scp -q \"${tmp_init}\" \"${PEER_ROOT}@${peer}:/etc/init.d/ollama\"\n    ssh \"${PEER_ROOT}@${peer}\" \"\n        set -e\n        chmod +x /etc/init.d/ollama\n        chown root:root /etc/init.d/ollama\n        rc-update add ollama default 2>/dev/null || true\n        rc-service ollama restart\n    \"\n\n    rm -f \"${tmp_serve}\" \"${tmp_init}\"\n    echo \"Peer ${peer} runtime ready.\"\n}\n# }}}",
          "old_string":"# {{{ provision_peer()\n# Set up the runtime on a peer over ssh. The peer ssh user is unprivileged,\n# so we stage files in /tmp and use doas for the install + service ops.\n# Requires the following one-time doas config on each peer:\n#\n#   echo \"permit nopass sora cmd /usr/bin/install\" >> /etc/doas.d/doas.conf\n#   echo \"permit nopass sora cmd /sbin/rc-update args add ollama default\" >> /etc/doas.d/doas.conf\n#   echo \"permit nopass sora cmd /sbin/rc-service args ollama restart\" >> /etc/doas.d/doas.conf\n#\n# Without those rules in place the doas calls below will prompt for a\n# password and the script will hang on the peer step.\nprovision_peer() {\n    local peer=\"$1\"\n    local bind_ip=\"$2\"\n    echo \"Provisioning ${peer} (bind ${bind_ip}:${OLLAMA_PORT})...\"\n\n    local tmp_serve\n    tmp_serve=\"$(mktemp)\"\n    emit_serve_sh \"${bind_ip}\" > \"${tmp_serve}\"\n\n    local tmp_init\n    tmp_init=\"$(mktemp)\"\n    emit_openrc_unit > \"${tmp_init}\"\n\n    scp -q \"${tmp_serve}\" \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}:${DIR}/serve.sh\"\n    scp -q \"${tmp_init}\" \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}:/tmp/ollama.init\"\n    rm -f \"${tmp_serve}\" \"${tmp_init}\"\n\n    ssh \"${PEER_USER}@${peer}\" \"\n        set -e\n        chmod +x ${DIR}/serve.sh\n        mkdir -p ${MODELS_DIR}\n        doas /usr/bin/install -m 755 -o root -g root /tmp/ollama.init /etc/init.d/ollama\n        rm -f /tmp/ollama.init\n        doas /sbin/rc-update add ollama default\n        doas /sbin/rc-service ollama restart\n    \"\n    echo \"Peer ${peer} runtime ready.\"\n}\n# }}}"
        },
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01SwfWnnCvykyFGUZrR7DyW2"
      }]
  },

Summary of what changed:\n\n## Config (top of script)\n\n```\nHOST_1_IP=\"192.168.1.11\"   HOST_1_PORT=\"10101\"\nHOST_2_IP=\"192.168.1.12\"   HOST_2_PORT=\"20202\"\nHOST_3_IP=\"192.168.1.13\"   HOST_3_PORT=\"30303\"\nPEER_USER=\"sora\"\nPEER_ROOT=\"root\"\n```\n\n## Auto-detect, no per-host script editing\n\nThe same script works on any of the three hosts. `detect_self_ip` walks the configured IPs against `ip -4 addr show` and picks whichever one is bound locally. From that, `port_for_ip` maps to the host's port. Peers become \"the other two configured IPs, in order.\"\n\n## How serve.sh gets the right values per host\n\n`emit_serve_sh` takes `(bind_ip, port)` and generates a `serve.sh` with those values **baked in as literal strings**. Each peer gets a serve.sh customized for it:\n\n- sora1 → `BIND_IP=\"192.168.1.11\"`, `PORT=\"10101\"`\n- sora2 → `BIND_IP=\"192.168.1.12\"`, `PORT=\"20202\"`\n- sora3 → `BIND_IP=\"192.168.1.13\"`, `PORT=\"30303\"`\n\nThe wrong serve.sh on the wrong host would fail noisily (Ollama tries to bind an IP not on the box).\n\n## Two ssh identities, no doas\n\n- **`sora@peer`** — binary tarball deploy, serve.sh placement under `/home/sora/programs/ollama/`, models directory creation.\n- **`root@peer`** — `/etc/init.d/ollama` install, `rc-update add`, `rc-service ollama restart`.\n\n## One-time setup per peer\n\nOn each peer (sora2, sora3), as root once:\n\n```\n# 1. Allow root ssh by key (no password)\nsed -i 's/^#*PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config\nrc-service sshd restart\n```\n\nThen from the build host:\n\n```\nssh-copy-id sora@192.168.1.12\nssh-copy-id root@192.168.1.12\nssh-copy-id sora@192.168.1.13\nssh-copy-id root@192.168.1.13\n```\n\nAfter that, all subsequent runs of `/tmp/ollama-build-and-deploy.sh` from any of the three hosts fully provision the other two with zero interactive prompts.\n\nRe-copy the script. The first run on each host will install/refresh the service and start it.
